summary: This note is a short biographical entry on Brantley York, a Methodist minister and educator. It states his full name, birth and death dates, and that he is best known for founding and serving as president of the institution that became Duke University, then called Union Institute Academy in Randolph County, North Carolina. It also notes he founded six schools in total.
one_line: Brantley York was a 19th-century Methodist minister and educator who founded Union Institute Academy, later Duke University, and six schools overall.
key_facts: Richard Brantley York was born on January 3, 1805.
Richard Brantley York died on October 7, 1891.
Brantley York was a Methodist minister and educator.
Brantley York is best known for founding the institution that would become Duke University.
That institution was called Union Institute Academy and was located in Randolph County, North Carolina.
Brantley York served as president of Union Institute Academy.
Brantley York founded six schools overall.
